svg.title: K26: an init container waits for a Service that does not exist
svg.desc: The Pod has an init container wait-for-redis whose loop tries to connect to redsi on port 6379, a typo of redis. Nothing is called redsi, so the loop never exits. Kubernetes only creates the app container after every init container finishes, so the app never starts: no logs, no restarts, status Init 0 of 1. The real Service redis is healthy but is never asked. The fix is to spell redis correctly.

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cats vs Dogs is waiting for its database. Forever.

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The app container starts only after every init container has finished

svg.text: Init containers run first, one at a time, and the app waits for all of them. A loop that never ends is a quiet hang.

svg.text: Pod stays Init:0/1 with 0 restarts. The app has no logs because it never started. Read the init container's logs.

svg.text: Correct the name in the init loop: redsi becomes redis. The init container exits, the app container starts.
